user_prompt: In older adults (≥55 years) with an anxiety or related disorder, what is the effect of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) compared with minimal management on dropout rates at 3–6 months post-treatment?  Evaluate ONLY dropout/discontinuation at 3–6 months post-treatment — not immediate post-treatment dropout. Minimal management may include waiting list, usual care, supportive/attention control, or medication without active psychological therapy; exclude comparisons against another active psychological therapy. Extract dropout events and total participants per arm, and pool using risk ratio (RR).  Dropout counts are often stated in narrative text rather than tables — read Results/Attrition/Sample-Selection sections carefully, not just tables. If a paper reports dropout in two explicitly-stated sequential intervals (e.g., "X by post-treatment, plus Y more by 6 months"), sum them for the cumulative total — this is arithmetic on stated numbers, not an estimate, and should not be left null. If multiple eligible follow-ups fall within the 3–6 month window, use the latest one. Exclude protocols and non-RCTs, and extract no other outcome.
